acceptance_rule: PIT trailing-only covariance AND regime (no lookahead). Compare static vs always-on overlay (exp-026) vs regime-conditioned overlay over 3 windows. Accept if aggregate EV (total_return x sharpe_daily) beats BOTH static and always-on overlay, with drawdown still reduced vs static in non-BULL windows. Frozen overlay params (cap 15pct, vol target 30pct); only the regime gate is new. Observed-only; production = discretionary risk policy.

hub_identity.reservation_rule: Reserve the ticket (atomic O_EXCL create) before writing runners, artifacts, data, or logs. Existing IDs are rejected across registry, JSONL, tickets, logs, artifacts, data, and runners.

hypothesis: Regime-conditioned held-book risk-budget overlay: apply the exp-20260623-026 overlay (15pct single-name risk cap + 30pct vol target, excess to cash) ONLY when the PIT market regime is NOT BULL, and hold static (full weights) when regime is BULL. Regime = production compute_market_regime() (SPY+QQQ vs 200d MA), evaluated PIT with trailing-only data at each monthly rebalance. Hypothesis: the gate keeps the drawdown protection in non-BULL windows while removing the bull-window return drag that made the always-on overlay EV-negative, so aggregate EV beats BOTH static and the always-on overlay. Observed-only; no core-strategy/order change.

novelty.new_evidence_axis: Adds a PIT 200d-MA market-regime GATE (existing production compute_market_regime, unchanged) on top of the rejected always-on overlay exp-20260623-026. The gate is the single new variable; thresholds of the underlying overlay are frozen at exp-026 values (not a sweep). Distinct from exp-026 (always-on) which was rejected for bull-window return drag.

prediction.confidence_reason: 200d MA regime is slow and may not cleanly separate the windows (late_strong had a big drawdown despite being a bull window); honest coin-flip whether the gate recovers EV vs the always-on overlay.

post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: The 200d-MA regime gate recovered most of the bull-window upside the always-on overlay discarded: aggregate EV nearly doubled vs always-on (18.6->29.1, mean return 29%->46%) while keeping partial drawdown protection (worst DD 44%->32% vs static -44%). But it still lost to static (EV 44.4) because static hold of these winners over overwhelmingly-bull windows is a brutal EV baseline, and the 200d MA gate is too slow - it had BEAR sub-periods inside bull windows (return cost) and stayed BULL through part of the old_thin drawdown (incomplete protection).
post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not sweep the regime gate (MA period, BULL definition) or the frozen overlay params toward old_thin - that curve-fits the one known-bad window. Cross-experiment lesson (exp-026 + this): no de-risking variant beats static hold on EV for this winner book over these bull windows.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: A genuinely different OBJECTIVE that prices tail risk explicitly (then always-on/regime overlays already win on drawdown), OR a structurally faster, independently-validated chop/regime signal (exp-019 efficiency-ratio chop state) tested without threshold tuning, OR a forward non-survivorship book. Not gate/param sweeps.
